detailed_description: The Random Number Generator is a cryptographic-grade tool that produces uniformly distributed integers within customizable ranges using a cryptographically secure pseudorandom number generator (CSPRNG). Unlike basic implementations relying on system time seeds, this tool incorporates entropy from hardware sources (when available) and employs AES-256-CTR_DRBG algorithms to ensure unpredictability. Developers can generate single values or bulk batches up to 10,000 numbers with precision controls for min/max bounds, duplicate prevention via Fisher-Yates shuffle validation, and optional seed replay functionality. The tool's uniqueness lies in its hybrid entropy model that combines OS-level randomness (via Crypto.getRandomValues() in browsers or getrandom() syscall on Linux) with user-provided seed entropy, making it suitable for security-sensitive applications. Use cases include generating test datasets for database stress-testing, creating cryptographically sound salts for password hashing, simulating dice rolls in gaming algorithms, and producing verifiable random sequences for blockchain applications. Output maintains strict numerical distribution compliance through chi-squared distribution testing before delivery.
usage_steps: Set integer boundaries using dual numeric inputs: specify minimum (-1,000,000 to 1,000,000) and maximum values
Configure batch parameters with quantity selector (1–10,000) and enable 'Unique Values Only' toggle for permutation-based output
Optional: Enter custom seed entropy (hexadecimal or base64) to reproduce specific sequences or verify randomness sources
Select output format: plain text, CSV column, or JSON array with configurable delimiter characters
Initiate generation with 'Cryptographic Entropy Boost' button to prioritize hardware entropy sources
Validate results through built-in statistical analysis panel showing distribution histograms and entropy metrics
usage_examples: Creating 200 unique API keys with 8-digit numerical components for rate-limiting tests
Simulating 10,000 dice rolls with 3-sided virtual dice for board game probability analysis
Generating 500MB of test data with controlled numerical variance for database index fragmentation studies
Producing verifiable randomness for NFT loot box algorithms requiring auditable entropy sources
